# The app, its context and the host

<!-- Generated by dist/sdk/gen-widget-docs.py from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

What an app implements (`UiApp`), what it is handed on every call (`UiCx`), the driver (`Host`), input events and the storage port.

## `app`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/app.rs`)

The app contract: three required calls. The same source builds native in the shell, as a WASM tile, and into the browser preview.

### enum `Flow`

What an app answers to an event.

```rust
pub enum Flow
```

Variants:

- `Stay`
- `Back`: Leave the app (back to the launcher).

### trait `UiApp`

```rust
pub trait UiApp
```

Methods:

- `fn id(&self) -> &'static str`: The app id (the dock, the launcher and the policy know it by this).
- `fn title(&self) -> String`
- `fn dock_status(&self) -> Option<DockStatus>  // has a default`: A badge and a status line for this app's dock icon, asked after every event.
- `fn wants_keyboard(&self) -> bool  // has a default`: True while the app has a text field in focus: the host shows the on-screen keyboard (a touch screen has no other way to type) and takes it away when this turns false. Asked after every event, like [`UiApp::dock_status`].
- `fn open_item(&mut self, _item: &str)  // has a default`: The shell opened this app because another app asked for one thing in it (the K8S tile asks the Terminal for a shell in a pod): plain text, never a secret. The default does nothing.
- `fn event(&mut self, ev: &UiEvent, cx: &mut UiCx) -> Flow`
- `fn view(&mut self, canvas: &mut dyn Canvas, cx: &UiCx)`: Draw the whole frame. Lay it out from `canvas.size()` and `cx.metrics()`.

## `cx`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/cx.rs`)

The context an app gets on every call: the Look, the screen, the pane, the view, the size class, and the dock and wallpaper ports.
Nothing here reaches the machine: an app that needs more gets it through a port of its own that the host hands it.

### struct `UiCx`

```rust
pub struct UiCx<'a>
```

Public fields:

- `pub look: &'a Look`
- `pub arrangement: &'a Arrangement`
- `pub pane: &'a Pane`
- `pub view: &'a ViewInfo`
- `pub touch: bool`
- `pub text_scale: f32`
- `pub now_ms: u64`: The host's clock at the last heartbeat, in milliseconds (0 before the first): for pacing, never for the date.
- `pub type_style: TypeStyle`
- `pub dock: &'a mut dyn DockPort`
- `pub wallpaper: &'a mut dyn WallpaperPort`

Methods:

- `pub fn colors(&self) -> &Theme`: The colours: always draw with these, never with a colour of your own (a lint test scans SDK apps for literals).
- `pub fn look(&self) -> &Look`
- `pub fn fonts(&self) -> TypeStyle`: The person's type choices: family, line height, letter spacing, tabular figures. Ask for a role (`FontRole`), never a file.
- `pub fn skin(&self) -> SkinInfo`: The skin in use: its key and name, whether it is dark, glass, reduced motion, and its shape, edge and spacing words. The person can switch it at any time; the next `view` call sees the new one (nothing restarts).
- `pub fn accent(&self, wanted: [u8; 4]) -> Accent`: The accent an app wants to ship, after the contrast check (WCAG AA: the label on it 4.5:1, it against the card and the page 3:1). An accent that fails is moved towards the skin's own, or replaced by it; `adjusted` says so.
- `pub fn colors_with_accent(&self, wanted: [u8; 4]) -> Theme`: The skin's colours with the app's accent fitted (a copy): draw with it and the widgets use the app's accent wherever it reads.
- `pub fn screen(&self) -> &Screen`: The screen this pane is on (the primary one when its own was unplugged).
- `pub fn pane(&self) -> &Pane`
- `pub fn view(&self) -> &ViewInfo`
- `pub fn size_class(&self) -> SizeClass`
- `pub fn metrics(&self) -> Metrics`
- `pub fn tokens(&self) -> Tokens`: The skin's numbers beyond colour (radii, borders, gaps, shadow, glass, glyph size, motion): read these, never write a number.
- `pub fn wallpaper_here(&self) -> wallpaper::Id`: The wallpaper of this pane's screen.
- `pub fn text_on_wallpaper(&self) -> [u8; 4]`: The colour for text drawn straight on this screen's wallpaper.

## `host`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/host.rs`)

The host: the one piece that drives an app on any target. It owns the app and its context data, turns raw pointers into gestures and
taps into actions (through the hit regions of the last frame), resizes and moves the pane, and publishes the dock status.
The desktop shell, the browser preview and the tests all use this same driver, so an app behaves the same everywhere.

### struct `Host`

```rust
pub struct Host<A: UiApp>
```

Public fields:

- `pub app: A`
- `pub look: Look`
- `pub arrangement: Arrangement`
- `pub pane: Pane`
- `pub view: ViewInfo`
- `pub touch: bool`
- `pub text_scale: f32`
- `pub type_style: TypeStyle`: The person's type choices (family, line height, letter spacing, tabular figures); the shell sets them from the core's settings.
- `pub dock: Box<dyn DockPort>`
- `pub wallpaper: Box<dyn WallpaperPort>`

Methods:

- `pub fn new(app: A, look: Look, arrangement: Arrangement, dock: Box<dyn DockPort>, wallpaper: Box<dyn WallpaperPort>) -> Host<A>`: The pane starts as the whole primary screen in the view "main".
- `pub fn event(&mut self, ev: &UiEvent) -> Flow`: Give the app one event.
- `pub fn action_at(&self, x: f32, y: f32) -> Option<u32>`: The action of the hit region of the last frame at a place: what a tap there would be told (the tile adapter uses it to tell a tap the host already resolved from the tile ABI's `Hit` event for the same tap).
- `pub fn wants_keyboard(&self) -> bool`: Whether the app wants the on-screen keyboard now (a field is in focus). The shell, the tile adapter and the browser read this after each event and show or hide the keyboard.
- `pub fn pointer(&mut self, p: Pointer) -> Flow`: A raw pointer: it goes to the app, and the gestures it makes follow; a tap on a hit region of the last frame is its `Action`.
- `pub fn tick(&mut self, now_ms: u64) -> Flow`: The clock moved on (long presses) and the heartbeat.
- `pub fn mouse(&mut self, x: f32, y: f32, phase: Phase, t_ms: u64) -> Flow`: Mouse press, release and move are `Pointer`s too (id 0).
- `pub fn resize(&mut self, w: f32, h: f32)`: The pane was resized (a window drag, a rotation).
- `pub fn move_to(&mut self, screen: u32, view: ViewInfo)`: The pane moved to another screen and view (size from the screen unless the caller resizes it after).
- `pub fn place(&mut self, pane: Pane, view: ViewInfo) -> bool`: The shell's pane manager says where this app is drawn now: the pane (screen, view, size in logical units) and the view's place in the person's views. `Resized` is sent only when something changed (so a still pane costs the app nothing). True when it did.
- `pub fn unplug_screen(&mut self, id: u32) -> bool`: A screen was unplugged: a pane that was on it moves back to the primary screen, so nothing is lost.
- `pub fn draw(&mut self, canvas: &mut dyn Canvas)`: Draw the frame on a canvas (the pane takes the canvas's size).
- `pub fn set_look(&mut self, look: Look)`: Draw the frame as a display list (what a browser or client gets) and keep it for hit testing. Switch the skin (the Look) live: the app keeps its state and the next frame is drawn with the new one. The person's choice per account is kept by the core (`look_registry`), not here.
- `pub fn set_type_style(&mut self, t: TypeStyle)`: The person's type choices changed (Settings): the next frame uses them.
- `pub fn record(&mut self) -> DisplayList`
- `pub fn set_last(&mut self, list: DisplayList)`: Remember a frame drawn some other way (the raster path records the same hits) for tap resolution.

## `event`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/event.rs`)

One input model for every target: pointer (with an id, so several fingers), wheel, keys, text, the actions of hit regions, resize and
the heartbeat. A mobile view is the same events with touch pointers; [`crate::gesture`] turns raw pointers into taps, long presses,
drags and swipes.

Variants:

- `Tap { x: f32, y: f32 }`
- `LongPress { x: f32, y: f32 }`
- `DragStart { x: f32, y: f32 }`
- `Drag { dx: f32, dy: f32 }`: The distance moved since the drag began.
- `DragEnd { dx: f32, dy: f32 }`
- `Swipe(Dir)`
- `Pinch { scale: f32, x: f32, y: f32 }`: Two fingers: the distance between them now over the distance when the second one came down (1.0 = unchanged), and the place half way between them.
- `PinchEnd { scale: f32 }`: A finger of the pinch lifted; the last scale.

### enum `UiEvent`

```rust
pub enum UiEvent
```

Variants:

- `Pointer(Pointer)`
- `Gesture(Gesture)`
- `Wheel(i32)`: Positive = towards older content.
- `Key(UiKey)`
- `Text(String)`: Text for the focused field (typed, pasted or composed by an input method).
- `Action(u32)`: A hit region was used (a click, a tap, Enter on a focused control).
- `Drop { from: u32, to: u32 }`: A drag that began on one hit region ended on another: the action of the region it was picked up from and the action of the region it was let go over (drag and drop; made by the host from the drag gestures and the last frame's hit regions, never sent by a client).
- `Resized`: The pane changed size, screen or view: ask `cx` again.
- `Tick`: About 30 times a second.

## `ports`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/ports.rs`)

Ports that carry no pixels: what an app keeps and how it asks for it. An SDK app never opens a file or a socket (the core rule): it is
handed a port, and the port is the core's. [`MemStorage`] is the in-memory one for tests and the browser preview; the core-backed one is
`iyakki-sdk-tile`'s `CoreStorage`, which asks the core's `storage` namespace (get, set, remove, list) through the tile ABI's `call`.

### const `STORAGE_LIMIT`

The most one app may keep, in bytes of keys and values together (the core's limit for `storage`).

```rust
pub const STORAGE_LIMIT: usize = 256 * 1024
```

### const `MAX_KEY`

The longest key and the longest value a port takes.

```rust
pub const MAX_KEY: usize = 128
```

### const `MAX_VALUE`

```rust
pub const MAX_VALUE: usize = 64 * 1024
```

### enum `PortError`

```rust
pub enum PortError
```

Variants:

- `BadKey`: The key or value is not acceptable (empty or too long key, too long value).
- `TooBig`: The app would keep more than [`STORAGE_LIMIT`].
- `Denied`: The core did not allow it or did not answer.

## `zoom`  (`crates/iyakki-ui-sdk/src/zoom.rs`)

`TextZoom`: the text size an app lets the person change with a pinch and with two buttons (F-SDK-26, F-SDK-34). The size is a thousandth of
the person's own text size (1000 is as set in the Look), kept between [`TextZoom::MIN`] and [`TextZoom::MAX`]. A pinch reports a scale since
the fingers landed, so the new size is counted from the size the pinch began at, not from the last report; the end of the pinch is the moment
to keep the size (one storage write, not one per report). An app that builds its [`crate::size::Metrics`] with [`TextZoom::metrics`] draws every
widget and view at the new size.

### enum `ZoomChange`

What a gesture did to the zoom.

```rust
pub enum ZoomChange
```

Variants:

- `None`: Not a pinch (or a scale that cannot be one): nothing happened.
- `Moving`: The size moved while the fingers are on the screen.
- `Ended`: The fingers lifted: the size is final, keep it.

### struct `TextZoom`

```rust
pub struct TextZoom
```

Methods:

- `pub fn from_text(t: Option<&str>) -> TextZoom`: The size kept as text (what [`TextZoom::keep_text`] gave); anything that is not a number is the start size, a number out of range is held inside it.
- `pub fn keep_text(&self) -> String`
- `pub fn milli(&self) -> u32`: The size as a thousandth of the person's own size.
- `pub fn factor(&self) -> f32`: The factor to multiply the person's text size with.
- `pub fn label(&self) -> String`: A short name for the size, for a screen reader: "Text size 115%".
- `pub fn set(&mut self, milli: u32)`
- `pub fn bigger(&mut self)`
- `pub fn smaller(&mut self)`
- `pub fn gesture(&mut self, g: &Gesture) -> ZoomChange`: A gesture: a pinch moves the size, the end of it fixes it. Every other gesture is none of this.
- `pub fn metrics(&self, cx: &crate::cx::UiCx) -> crate::size::Metrics`: The pane's metrics with the person's own text size and this zoom applied (what `UiCx::metrics` gives, at the zoomed size).
